source_name: registeruz.sk – official register of financial statements (SK entities)
why_relevant: Statutory filings for every SK-registered PSP/acquirer entity (e.g. Global Payments s.r.o., organizačná zložka IČO 50010301; Global Payments Europe organizačná zložka) — the only public way to size local revenue, headcount and trajectory of payments competitors.

source_name: FinStat.sk – SK company financial/ownership aggregator
why_relevant: Aggregates registeruz + obchodný register into ready-made revenue/profit time series and ownership/officer changes per SK payments entity (also flags dissolved entities such as Global Payments Europe Slovakia v likvidácii). Faster than raw filings, but derived — and the free tier is limited.

source_name: Slovenská sporiteľňa – Global Payments partner/bank acquiring channel page
why_relevant: Concrete example of the bank-distribution model for acquiring in SK: the bank fronts a third-party acquirer to its business customers, with joint promotions. Equivalent pages at other SK banks (Tatra banka CardPay, VÚB eCard) map the whole bank-acquiring layer.

source_name: Shoptet Pay support – supported payment methods (SK)
why_relevant: E-commerce platforms reveal the payments estate indirectly: which PSPs/methods a dominant SK/CZ shop platform embeds is a strong proxy for SME gateway market share. Same logic applies to other platform integration directories.

source_name: PaymentProviders.io / PayAtlas – international PSP directories with SK country pages
why_relevant: English-language aggregator directories offering SK-filtered provider lists and country compliance/fee overviews; useful for cross-checking the domestic actor map and for spotting cross-border PSPs targeting SK merchants. Directory accuracy is uneven — validate against the NBS register.

source_name: FINAS – Fintech & Insurtech Association of Slovakia (membership directory)
why_relevant: FINAS site states 70+ member companies spanning payments, blockchain, banking software, consulting and insurtech (named examples seen: VISA, 365.bank, Akcenta, Crypto Voucher, ANASOFT, DigFin, FinReg Partners). A member roster exposes an entire cohort of SK payments actors and their partners in one place, years before some appear in statutory registers.

source_name: NBS Innovation Hub (Inovačný hub NBS pre oblasť fintech)
why_relevant: Launched Apr 2019 with the Ministry of Finance; the regulator's single front door for fintech entrants (crowdfunding, virtual assets, mobile payment apps). Firms that consult the hub are typically pre-licence competitors — the hub's existence and its intake themes flag where new SK payments activity is forming.

source_name: NBS Innovation Hub – Activity Report series (Správa o činnosti inovačného hubu)
why_relevant: Periodic regulator report on what kinds of firms and use-cases approached the hub. Best available structured read on the pipeline of not-yet-licensed SK fintech/paytech entrants and on which business models NBS is being asked about.

source_name: NBS regulačný sandbox (regulatory sandbox / pieskovisko inovácií)
why_relevant: Launched early 2022 on top of the innovation hub; sandbox participants are named, licensable-in-progress fintechs — the earliest formal public signal that a new payments competitor intends to operate in SK.

source_name: NBS register of supervised entities (Subjekty finančného trhu)
why_relevant: Authoritative register of SK-supervised financial-market entities; the confirmation layer for every startup/association-member name discovered elsewhere, and where EU-passported entrants operating via branch appear. Complements the payment-institutions/AISP listing.

source_name: Revolut Slovensko – SK market site and Revolut Bank governance pages
why_relevant: Flagship EU-passported entrant in SK. The sk-SK product pages and the Revolut Bank UAB leadership/governance page document the SK product surface (accounts, transfers) and the licence path (ECB licence, supervised by Bank of Lithuania) — i.e. exactly how a passported competitor reaches SK customers without a SK licence.

source_name: Tracxn – FinTech startups in Slovakia (222-company sector explorer)
why_relevant: Largest single enumerated SK fintech cohort found (222 companies, 36 funded, 10 Series A+, ~$37.2M raised, 5 acquisitions, 2 IPOs; names surfaced include Inforbus, Finax, Blockmate, Innovatrics, VESTBERRY, TrustPay, Datamolino, DigFin). Ideal seed list to snowball into ORSR/NBS.

source_name: Crunchbase Slovakia hubs (startups, companies, investors, software)
why_relevant: Canonical SK country slice for funding rounds and investor graphs; the investors hub in particular maps which VCs back SK paytech, which then leads to their portfolio pages (a second-order pointer).

source_name: SAPIE – Slovak Alliance for Innovation Economy (member base, 180+ orgs)
why_relevant: Represents 180+ members: innovative companies, startups, VC funds, angel investors, coworkings and accelerators. Broader than fintech but the single best cross-cutting pointer to SK funders/accelerators whose portfolios contain paytech, and the publisher of the first Slovak innovator map.

source_name: Innovation Map Slovakia (innovationmapslovakia.sk) – accelerators, funding, networks
why_relevant: Online database of SK innovation-ecosystem players categorised into network / support / education / funding, with a dedicated Accelerators & Incubators section. Directly satisfies the 'accelerators and VC portfolios' half of this cell.

source_name: Startup Report Slovensko (Slovenská sporiteľňa + Civitta; SASK edition)
why_relevant: Annual survey of the SK startup ecosystem (2025 edition: 183 startups, 41 investors) produced by a systemic bank with a consultancy. Gives cohort-level funding, sector split and investor sentiment — and the bank's own involvement is itself a bank/fintech partnership signal.

source_name: Crowdberry investment platform (SK/CZ growth capital, SLSP shareholder)
why_relevant: SK/CZ investment marketplace with two growth funds and ~19+ portfolio companies; Slovenská sporiteľňa became a shareholder — a documented bank–alternative-finance partnership. Portfolio pages are a pointer to fundable SK companies, and the bank tie-up is a case study in itself.

source_name: Slovak Investment Holding (SIH) / state-backed fund-of-funds startup investments
why_relevant: The state channel funding SK fintech: SIH invested EUR 1.4m into payments fintech Veslo (total round EUR 2m with a private co-investor); reporting also describes EUR 33m of state startup money placed with private funds. SIH announcements name specific paytech competitors early and identify which private funds manage the money.

source_name: Startitup.sk – startup section
why_relevant: High-volume SK startup media; carried the Veslo/SIH payments-platform funding story and routine profiles of SK founders. Useful as a broad early-signal net, lower precision than Forbes.

source_name: FinStat.sk – SK company financials and registry mirror
why_relevant: Resolves any discovered SK fintech or association name to IČO, filings, revenue and ownership (example: Slovenská FinTech asociácia, IČO 51910497). The workhorse for converting a startup-database or association name into a verifiable legal entity, and for sizing very small paytech firms that no VC database covers.

source_name: Ministry of Finance SR – Financial Innovation section
why_relevant: MF SR co-founded the NBS innovation hub and owns national fintech-strategy work (FINAS runs a National Fintech Strategy working group). Policy documents here set the licensing and open-banking direction that new SK entrants respond to.

source_name: CEE Fintech Atlas – Slovak fintech ecosystem country profile
why_relevant: Regional CEE fintech mapping initiative with a dedicated SK ecosystem write-up; useful for cross-country benchmarking and for named-actor recall, though the entry found dates to 2021 and needs freshness checks.

source_name: LinkedIn company pages of SK fintech associations and members
why_relevant: FINAS, SFA and SAPIE post member announcements, onboarding of new members and event partners on LinkedIn (member mentions observed include AD Strategies, ANASOFT, Enehano DigFin). Often the fastest public signal that a firm has joined the ecosystem or partnered with a bank.

source_name: Podnikajte.sk / Podnikam.sk – Slovenské startupy sections and funding-programme guides
why_relevant: SK SME/business portals that catalogue startup profiles and, importantly, the grant and financing programmes available in a given year — the funding-instrument side of who can afford to enter SK paytech.

source_name: UVP TECHNICOM (Košice) – university science park / fintech hub node
why_relevant: Regional incubator/science park that relays NBS fintech-hub information to its resident startups; incubator resident lists are a pointer to very early-stage SK fintech outside Bratislava, a segment invisible in VC databases.
